subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
title: Listening and Speaking: Pronunciation and Vocabulary
overview: Family celebrations use words such as birthday, party, gift and joy. In this sub-strand you will hear and say the sounds /ɜː/, /ɑː/, /ɔɪ/, /aɪ/, /l/ and /r/, build celebration words, and use them in clear sentences.

lessons.title: Hearing the sounds /ɜː/, /ɑː/, /ɔɪ/ and /aɪ/
objectives: Say words that contain each target sound.
Match celebration words to the sound they contain.
lessons.intro: The words boy and buy are easy to mix up if you hurry. Boy names a male child. Buy means to pay for something. The vowel sound in the middle is what keeps the two words apart.
lessons.notes:
### Sounds, not just letters
In this lesson a sound is written between slanting lines, like /ɔɪ/. The lines mean we are talking about what we hear, not about one spelling. The same sound can be spelled in more than one way.

### /ɜː/ as in birthday
/ɜː/ is the long vowel in bird, girl, birthday, turn, word and her. Your mouth is relaxed and the sound is held. You often see it spelled ir (birthday, girl), ur (turn, church), or (word) or er (her).

Say: birthday, girl, turn, her, church.

### /ɑː/ as in father
/ɑː/ is the long "ah" in father, party, card and start. Open your mouth and keep the sound long. You often see it spelled ar (card, start, arm) or a (father, party).

Say: father, party, card, start.

Do not swap /ɜː/ and /ɑː/. Birthday has /ɜː/. Party has /ɑː/. They are different vowels even though both can be long.

### /ɔɪ/ as in boy
/ɔɪ/ glides. Start with the vowel in "or" and move toward the vowel in "see". You hear it in boy, toy, joy, coin and voice. The usual spellings are oy (boy, toy, joy) and oi (coin, voice).

### /aɪ/ as in prize
/aɪ/ also glides. Start with "ah" and move toward "ee". You hear it in my, prize, invite, time and night. Spellings include i (prize, invite, time), y (my) and igh (night).

### Hear the difference
- boy /ɔɪ/ and buy /aɪ/
- toy /ɔɪ/ and tie /aɪ/
- birthday /ɜː/ and party /ɑː/

### Celebration words with these vowels
- birthday, church (/ɜː/)
- party, father, card (/ɑː/)
- boy, toy, joy (/ɔɪ/)
- invite, prize, night (/aɪ/)

When you listen to a story about a party, tap once for /ɔɪ/ and twice for /aɪ/. Training your ear is the first step to saying the words clearly.

keyWords.meaning: the long vowel sound in birthday, bird and turn
the long ah sound in father, party and card
the vowel sound in boy, toy and joy
the vowel sound in my, prize and invite

examples.problem: Which word has /ɔɪ/: boy, buy or card?
steps: Boy has the oy spelling and the /ɔɪ/ sound.
Buy has /aɪ/. Card has /ɑː/.

examples.problem: Sort these words by vowel sound: birthday, party, joy, prize.
steps: Birthday has /ɜː/.
Party has /ɑː/.
Joy has /ɔɪ/.
Prize has /aɪ/.

activity.title: Listen and sort the vowels
materials: A list of words read aloud by the teacher or played from an audio recording
steps: Listen to each word once: birthday, girl, party, father, card, boy, toy, joy, invite, prize, night, turn.
Point to the card for the vowel sound you hear. Do not look at a spelling until you have chosen.
Say the word after the teacher, matching the length of the vowel.
With a partner, say boy and buy, then toy and tie, and explain the meaning of each word.

practice.question: Write the sound symbol for the vowel in joy.
Which word does not have /aɪ/: invite, prize, night, coin?
Say whether birthday and party have the same vowel sound. Name both sounds.
practice.answer: No. Birthday has /ɜː/ and party has /ɑː/.

practice.question: What is the difference in meaning between boy and buy?
practice.answer: A boy is a male child. To buy is to pay for something.

summary: /ɜː/ is the vowel in birthday. /ɑː/ is the vowel in father and party.
/ɔɪ/ is the vowel in boy and joy. /aɪ/ is the vowel in prize and invite.
Hear the sound before you worry about the spelling.

lessons.title: The sounds /l/ and /r/ and celebration words
objectives: Hear and say /l/ and /r/ at the beginning of words.
Use word wheels to build words such as load and road.
Explain celebration words and use four of them in sentences.
lessons.intro: If someone says "Turn light at the gate" when they mean "Turn right", the visitor walks the wrong way. The sounds /l/ and /r/ are different, and a celebration direction can depend on them.
lessons.notes:
### How to make /l/
Put the tip of your tongue on the ridge behind your top teeth and let the air pass along the sides. Your voice is on. You hear /l/ at the start of load, light, play, balloon, colourful and celebrate.

### How to make /r/
Keep the tongue tip from touching that ridge. The tongue pulls back a little and the voice stays on. You hear /r/ at the start of road, right, pray, ribbon, present and prize.

Do not press your lips together for either sound. If /r/ starts to sound like /w/, smile slightly and keep the tongue busy.

### Pairs that change meaning
- load and road
- light and right
- play and pray
- glass and grass
- lock and rock

Load means to put things onto a vehicle or a table. Road means the way vehicles travel. A wedding party can load gifts into a car and then travel on the road. Both words matter.

### Word wheels
A word wheel has a sound in the centre and letters around the edge. Join the centre to different letters to make words.

- Centre /l/: load, light, lock
- Centre /r/: road, right, rock
- Centre /ɔɪ/: boy, toy, joy
- Centre /aɪ/: my can be built by adding letters around the sound in prize, invite and night

### Words for family celebrations
- celebrate: to mark a special day with happy activities
- ceremony: a set of formal actions for an important event
- invitation: a request, spoken or written, asking someone to come
- wedding: the ceremony when two people marry
- birthday: the day each year that marks when a person was born
- burial: the ceremony of laying to rest a person who has died. Families gather, sing and comfort one another.
- feast: a large special meal
- graduation: a ceremony at the end of a level of school
- baptise: in many Christian families, a ceremony that welcomes a person, often a baby, with water
- decorate: to make a place look special
- Other useful words: ribbon, balloon, gift, present, card, cake, prize, song, joy

A present and a gift can mean the same thing: something you give. A prize is something you win.

Use a word in a full sentence so its meaning shows: We will decorate the room with balloons and ribbons for the birthday party.

keyWords.meaning: a set of formal actions for an important event such as a wedding
a request asking someone to come to an event
a large special meal for a celebration
to add colours and objects that make a place look special

examples.problem: Which word begins with /r/: balloon, ribbon, colourful, celebrate?
steps: Balloon, colourful and celebrate begin with other sounds or have /l/.
Ribbon begins with /r/.

examples.problem: Use invitation and feast in one sentence about a wedding.
steps: An invitation asks people to come.
A feast is the special meal.
Join them with a wedding.
examples.answer: Our invitation to the wedding said there would be a feast after the ceremony.

activity.title: Word wheels for /l/ and /r/
steps: In a group, draw two wheels. Write /l/ in the centre of one and /r/ in the centre of the other.
Around /l/ write load, light, lock, balloon and play. Around /r/ write road, right, rock, ribbon and prize.
Say each pair, load/road and light/right, and point to the wheel you hear when a partner says one word.
Choose four celebration words and each say a sentence that uses one of them.

practice.question: Write the /r/ partner of load, light and lock.
What is the difference between a gift and a prize?
practice.answer: A gift is something you give to someone. A prize is something a person wins.

practice.question: Use the word decorate in a sentence about a birthday.
practice.answer: Any correct sentence, for example: We will decorate the room with balloons for the birthday party.

summary: /l/ touches the tooth ridge. /r/ does not.
Pairs such as load and road change meaning when the first sound changes.
Celebration words include ceremony, invitation, feast, decorate, gift and prize.

lessons.title: Clear words in a celebration dialogue
objectives: Pronounce target sounds in a short dialogue.
Say why a wrong sound can confuse a listener.
Role-play a celebration using the new words.
lessons.intro: A family is planning a birthday. Every person in the plan must be heard correctly: who to invite, what to buy, and where to put the ribbons. Clear sounds keep the plan from falling apart.
lessons.notes:
### A dialogue to listen to
Ask your teacher or a partner to read this aloud. Listen for /ɜː/, /ɑː/, /ɔɪ/, /aɪ/, /l/ and /r/.

Mother: We will have a party for your birthday.
Amina: May I invite my friends?
Mother: Yes. We can decorate the room with balloons and ribbons.
Father: I will buy a card and a gift. I will not forget the prize for the game.
Amina: Will there be a cake?
Mother: Yes, and we will sing a song. It will be a day of joy.
Father: Load the chairs onto the path, then carry them to the right side of the yard.

### Sounds in the dialogue
- party /ɑː/, birthday /ɜː/
- invite /aɪ/, buy /aɪ/, prize /aɪ/, right /aɪ/ and /r/
- joy /ɔɪ/
- balloons /l/, load /l/
- ribbons /r/, prize /r/, right /r/

Say the dialogue slowly, then at a natural speed. If you add the line "The boy will buy the balloons", keep boy and buy distinct.

### Why clear pronunciation matters
A listener cannot see your spelling. They only hear sounds. Load and road, light and right, boy and buy are different messages. At a celebration, the wrong word can send people, gifts or chairs to the wrong place.

Clear speech also shows respect. Guests who are older, younger, or visiting from another place should not have to struggle to understand you. Everyone's voice is a little different, and that is welcome. What we aim for is that the important sounds stay distinct.

### Subjects in these sentences
The key question for this theme also asks which words are used as subjects. In "Amina will invite her friends", Amina is the subject: she does the action. In "Father will buy a card", Father is the subject. The subject is usually the person or thing the sentence is about, and it often comes before the verb. Naming the subject clearly is part of speaking so that others understand.

### After you speak
When you role-play, face your partners, speak loudly enough for the group, and leave a pause at the full stop. If someone mishears right as light, repeat the word once, kindly, and show the direction with your hand.

keyWords.meaning: a conversation written so that each speaker has a turn
the person or thing that does the action in a sentence
to say a sound or word in a particular way

examples.problem: In the dialogue, who is the subject of "I will buy a card and a gift"?
steps: The speaker of that line is Father.
I stands for Father.
Father is the person who will buy.

examples.problem: A learner says "Turn light" but means the opposite of left. Which word should be used, and which sound starts it?
steps: The opposite of left in a direction is right.
Right begins with /r/ and has the vowel /aɪ/.

activity.title: Role-play the birthday plan
materials: Simple props such as a card, a ribbon or a paper balloon
A phone or tablet only if the teacher is recording
steps: Listen to the dialogue read aloud or played from an audio recording. List five words with the target sounds.
In groups of three, take the parts of Mother, Amina and Father and read the dialogue.
Add two new sentences that use celebration words, with a clear subject in each.
Role-play the scene. If the teacher agrees, record a short video and watch it to check the sounds /l/ and /r/ and the vowels /ɔɪ/ and /aɪ/.
Tell the class why saying load and road differently matters.

practice.question: Name the target vowel in party and the target vowel in birthday.
From the dialogue, write one word with /l/ and one word with /r/.
practice.answer: Any correct pair, for example balloons (/l/) and ribbons (/r/).

practice.question: Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly at a celebration?
practice.answer: So that listeners understand the right message. One wrong sound can change the word, as in light and right.

practice.question: Who is the subject in "Amina will invite her friends"?

summary: The dialogue practises /ɜː/, /ɑː/, /ɔɪ/, /aɪ/, /l/ and /r/ in real celebration words.
A changed sound can change the meaning, so listeners need clear speech.
The subject is the person or thing that the sentence is about.

quiz.question: Which word has the vowel /ɔɪ/?
quiz.explanation: Boy has /ɔɪ/. Prize has /aɪ/, card has /ɑː/, and birthday has /ɜː/.

quiz.question: Which pair contrasts /l/ and /r/?
quiz.explanation: Load begins with /l/ and road begins with /r/.

quiz.question: Which word begins with /r/?
quiz.explanation: Ribbon begins with /r/. The other words contain /l/.

quiz.question: The vowel in invite is ____.
quiz.explanation: Invite has the glide /aɪ/, the same vowel as prize and night.

quiz.question: What does feast mean?
options: A prize won in a game
quiz.explanation: A feast is a large special meal, often part of a celebration.

quiz.question: Choose the sentence that uses invitation correctly.
options: We ate the invitation with a spoon.
The invitation asked us to come to the wedding.
He kicked the invitation into the goal.
The invitation was a tall tree.
quiz.explanation: An invitation asks someone to attend an event.

quiz.question: Why does saying light instead of right cause a problem?
quiz.answer: The listener hears a different word and may go the wrong way or misunderstand the message.
quiz.explanation: Light and right are different words because /l/ and /r/ are different sounds.

quiz.question: Who is the subject in "Father will buy a card"?
quiz.explanation: Father is the person who does the action.

quiz.question: Which word has /ɜː/?
quiz.explanation: Girl has /ɜː/, like birthday and turn.

quiz.question: Why is clear pronunciation a sign of respect at a family celebration?
quiz.answer: Guests can understand you without struggling, including people who are younger, older or visiting.
quiz.explanation: The aim is distinct sounds so the message is easy to follow.
